beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You have watched this war from before the world to the restored kingdom. Three episodes left. First: where is the war right now? Answer — in your pocket. In your feed. In your head. Same two speeches. Modern clothes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Refresh the originals. One voice: Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever. The other: I will save them all — force them all — wherefore give me thine honor. Keep both in your ear, and listen to your day.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The devil's speech today almost never says worship me. It says: you deserve this. Skip the cost. Everyone does it. It hurts nobody. And its masterpiece line — there is no devil; that idea is medieval. Nephi transcribed that exact pitch twenty-five centuries early:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And behold, others he flattereth away, and telleth them there is no hell; and he saith unto them: I am no devil, for there is none — and thus he whispereth in their ears, until he grasps them with his awful chains, from whence there is no deliverance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I am no devil, for there is none. His best trick was never possession. It is public relations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And there is a second track, for the comfortable:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And others will he pacify, and lull them away into carnal security, that they will say: All is well in Zion; yea, Zion prospereth, all is well — and thus the devil cheateth their souls, and leadeth them away carefully down to hell.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Carefully. Not dramatically — carefully. No horns. No contracts at midnight crossroads. Just comfort, a closed curtain, and one degree of drift a day.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Now the Father's speech in modern clothes. His style guide is actually written down — how power from heaven is allowed to operate, and the only way:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: No power or influence can or ought to be maintained by virtue of the priesthood, only by persuasion, by long-suffering, by gentleness and meekness, and by love unfeigned.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Persuasion. Long-suffering. Gentleness. Love unfeigned. That is not just a rule for priesthood holders — it is the signature of heaven. So when any voice pushes, panics, shames, or forces you — check the return address.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Here is the whole field guide in one test, from Mormon. Does a thing invite you to do good, to love God, to serve? Or does it entice you to hurt, to despair, to quit? Every voice in your day sorts into those two bins — every ad, every impulse, every three-a.m. thought:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: That which is of God inviteth and enticeth to do good continually; wherefore, every thing which inviteth and enticeth to do good, and to love God, and to serve him, is inspired of God.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And the council replays daily, in small. Every time you choose the harder right with your freedom intact, you re-cast your vote from before the world. And every time something tries to control you for your own good — a manipulator, an addiction, an algorithm — that is the other speech, still hunting a throne.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You are not watching this war on a screen. You are in the cast. And your Father's side still fights exactly the way it fought in heaven — testimony, patience, love, and never, ever force. Choose like you chose. You have done this before.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: Every ad, impulse, and three-a.m. thought sorts into two speeches. You have voted before. Vote again.
